newsitem.title: USA: FCC has power to regulate liquor ads -- Hundt.
newsitem.headline: FCC has power to regulate liquor ads -- Hundt.

text.p: The head of the Federal Communications Commission insisted Tuesday his agency has the power to regulate television and radio advertising for hard liquor.

FCC Chairman Reed Hundt's comments come after two colleagues, Commissioners James Quello and Rachelle Chong, voiced doubts over the FCC's authority to oversee broadcast liquor ads. Quello said Monday it was up to Congress to change the laws and he called on lawmakers to do so next year.

"If the public interest would be served by our inquiry into the use of the airwaves by the hard-liquor industry and broadcasters who carry their ads, then we have no excuse for inaction," Hundt said in a speech to the Children's Action Network in Los Angeles.
"There is no doubt whatsoever about the FCC's jurisdiction in this area."

The debate surfaced after the distilled spirits industry earlier this month ended its decades-old voluntary ban on broadcast advertising. The ban has been in place since 1936 for radio and 1948 for TV.
Seagram Co. Ltd. in June began airing TV ads for its Royal Crown whiskey in selected local markets.
Hundt again called on TV stations to reject the ads, leaving open the possibility of FCC action if they did not do so.
